stories.title: Prince Harry makes surprise two‑day visit to Lviv to meet injured Ukrainian veterans
stories.summary: Prince Harry spent two days in Lviv, Ukraine, where he met injured service men and women, including Ukrainian competitors in his Invictus Games, and watched a wheelchair‑rugby match. He told the audience “You’re going to win the war” and toured projects that support treatment and rehabilitation for the country’s more than 150,000 wounded veterans. A press blackout was kept until he left the country, which continues to face missile attacks from Russia.
stories.why: This matters because it could expand treatment options or demonstrate a clinically meaningful new medical technology.

stories.title: India’s unemployment rate eases to 4.9% in October
stories.summary: Government data released on Monday show that the unemployment rate for people aged 15 and above fell to 4.9% in October, down from 5.0% in September and below the 5.1% forecast in a Reuters poll. The figures represent a 0.1‑percentage‑point decline from the previous month.
stories.why: The modest decline may ease labour‑market pressure, informing policymakers and investors about the health of the Indian economy.

stories.title: Independent MP Helen Haines released from hospital after alleged car attack
stories.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines was released from hospital four weeks after being struck by a vehicle in an alleged attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north‑east of Melbourne, on 19 October. The attack left her a double amputee, and she said she is “full of gratitude” upon discharge.
stories.why: The incident raises concerns about the safety of elected officials and the risk of politically‑motivated violence.
stories.previousTitle: Australian MP Helen Haines discharged after losing both legs in alleged car attack
stories.previousSummary: Independent MP Helen Haines, who lost both legs after a white Toyota LandCruiser was driven into her outside her Wangaratta electorate office on 19 October, has been released from hospital. stories.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi raises $24 million seed round for AI image sensors
stories.summary: Bharat Semi, a nearly five‑year‑old pre‑revenue semiconductor startup in New Delhi, announced a $24 million seed funding round to develop programmable AI‑enabled image sensors. The company says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense firm General Atomics and Indian firm Kaynes Semicon, and aims to begin commercial production in 2027. Co‑founder Vrinda Kapoor claims the sensors could reduce system costs by at least 70 % versus conventional sensor‑processor‑SoC configurations.
stories.why: The capital could help India expand its domestic chip ecosystem and offer cost‑effective AI vision solutions to global customers.
stories.previousTitle: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi raises $24 million seed round for AI image sensors
